record.original_question: If Y is a smooth convex billiard table and the billiard flow on Y is an integrable Hamiltonian system with two degrees of freedom, must Y be an ellipse?

evidence.quote: The billiard flow on a smooth, convex table Y is a Hamiltonian system with 2 degrees of freedom.
Problem 1a. Let Y be a smooth, convex billiard table. If the billiard flow on Y is an integrable Hamiltonian system, then Y is an ellipse.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth, strictly convex domain with smooth boundary $\partial Y$. The billiard flow inside $Y$ is the dynamical system describing a point particle that moves in straight lines inside $Y$ and reflects elastically off $\partial Y$ (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). This flow can be realized as a Hamiltonian system with two degrees of freedom; equivalently, the associated billiard map on the cylinder of inward-pointing unit tangent vectors based at $\partial Y$ preserves a smooth area form.

The billiard flow on $Y$ is called (Liouville-)integrable if there exists a smooth first integral, functionally independent of the energy on an open set of full measure, that is invariant under the billiard map (so that the phase space is foliated, away from a singular set, by invariant curves on which the dynamics is conjugate to a rotation).

Prove or disprove: if the billiard flow on $Y$ is integrable in the above sense, then $\partial Y$ is an ellipse.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical Birkhoff conjecture on integrable convex billiards. The full conjecture remains open. Important partial results include: Bialy's theorem (if all of phase space is foliated by invariant curves, the table is a disk); Avila–De Simoi–Kaloshin (nearly circular integrable domains are ellipses, 2016); Kaloshin–Sorrentino's local Birkhoff conjecture for perturbations of ellipses (Annals of Math, 2018); and Bialy–Mironov's result for centrally symmetric domains and Kaloshin et al.'s extension to nearly centrally symmetric domains (GAFA, 2024). The general (non-perturbative) case is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the Local Birkhoff Conjecture for Convex Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: The Birkhoff conjecture states that the boundary of a strictly convex integrable billiard table is necessarily an ellipse... it remains still open.
status_evidence.claim: The full Birkhoff conjecture is still open; a local perturbative version near ellipses is proved.

status_evidence.title: Nearly circular domains which are integrable close to the boundary are ellipses
status_evidence.snippet: Nearly circular integrable domains are ellipses.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: near-circular integrable domains are ellipses.

status_evidence.title: Birkhoff Conjecture for Nearly Centrally Symmetric Domains
status_evidence.snippet: A domain close enough to a centrally symmetric one with integrable billiard is an ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress for nearly centrally symmetric domains.
